summary: Home router PMTU/ICMP blocking causes split-tunnel VPN sessions to stall on corporate routes
description: Several remote employees report intermittent failures when accessing internal services while connected to corporate WireGuard split-tunnel VPN. Symptoms are consistent with TCP connections establishing but stalling on large transfers. Affected users are on a variety of consumer home routers that appear to block ICMP "destination unreachable"/fragmentation-needed messages which prevents Path MTU Discovery from completing. This causes MSS/PMTU blackholing and traffic to internal subnets to hang after initial handshake.
impact: 5-8 users reporting repeated slow/stalled sessions to internal APIs and git operations while on home networks. No broader office or datacenter impact reported. Affects internal-support and engineering teams working remotely; productivity degradation for large uploads, repo clones, and some RPC calls.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Connect remote client to corporate WireGuard split-tunnel (routes: 10.40.0.0/16 -> WG, default route remains local),
2) From remote client start a large HTTPS download or git clone from internal-host (MTU 9000 on internal side for dedicated link),
3) Observe handshake completes, then transfer stalls after ~1-2MB transferred,
4) Run tcpdump on client and capture shows repeated small MSS packets and no ICMP fragmentation-needed responses from path
5) On affected home router UI, verify ICMP/PMTU filtering or NAT handling (some routers expose 'Block ICMP' option).
observed_behavior: Connections to internal services establish (TCP handshake succeeds) but data transfer stalls. Wireshark/tcpdump shows retransmits from client, MSS clamping at low size, and no ICMP 'fragmentation needed' replies from upstream path. When user sets local interface MTU to 1400 or enables MSS clamping on WireGuard peer on client, transfers resume immediately.
expected_behavior: Path MTU Discovery should function across the home router path so split-tunnel VPN traffic to internal endpoints with larger MTU can flow without manual clamping. WireGuard should negotiate working MTU or fallback gracefully for the route.
logs:
2026-03-09T09:22:11Z client tcpdump: IP 192.168.1.50.52000 > 10.40.12.34.443: Flags [P.], seq 12345:14567, ack 6789, win 64240, length 2222
2026-03-09T09:22:11Z client retransmit: seq 12345:14567, retransmission after 200ms
router syslog: kernel: iptables REJECT ICMP type 3 code 4 -- policy 'Block ICMP' enabled
wireguard peer conf: MTU=1420, persistent-keepalive=25
investigation_notes: Initial triage: multiple reports from different ISPs and router vendors (Netgear, TP-Link, ISP-modems). Pattern points to home NAT/firewall blocking ICMP type 3 code 4 (fragmentation needed).
Reproduced locally with a GL-iNet consumer router by toggling 'Block ICMP' — enabling block replicates stall. Disabling allows PMTU discovery and transfers succeed.

Workaround validated: set interface MTU to 1350 on client or add 'MTU=1280' to WireGuard config on client — restores connectivity. Also validated server-side MSS clamping on edge LB (iptables --clamp-mss-to-pmtu) resolves symptoms for affected users without client changes.

Hypothesis: consumer routers that implement aggressive ICMP filtering or incorrect NAT PMTU handling drop fragmentation-needed messages from internal hosts, preventing PMTU recalculation on client and causing large packets to be dropped en route.
comments: 2026-03-10 10:12 - Aisha Patel: User reported repeated hangs when pushing a large Docker image to internal registry. Attached tcpdump and router model (Netgear R6700). User workaround: set 'Network > WAN > Fragmentation' disabled (unavailable on many routers).

2026-03-10 13:45 - Liam O'Connor: Reproduced with TP-Link Archer C7 in lab. Confirmed ICMP type 3 code 4 is filtered by default in firmware v1.1.1. Proposed fix: enable MSS clamp on edge load balancer and add note to remote VPN runbook.

2026-03-11 09:02 - SRE (Nadia Chen): Deployed iptables rule on lb-internal-1: -A FORWARD -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu on 2026-03-11T08:50Z in staging; will roll to prod after verification window.

2026-03-11 15:30 - Customer Success (Tom Ruiz): Notified impacted teams with workaround steps (client MTU/MSS clamping) and link to this ticket. Collecting list of affected employees for targeted follow-up.
2026-03-12 11:20 - Liam O'Connor: Prod rollout started. Monitor dashboards for increased retransmits on 10.40.0.0/16; no regressions observed in first 1 hour.
resolution: Workaround + short-term mitigation implemented: edge LB MSS clamping deployed to prod to mitigate clients with ICMP filtering. User-facing guidance updated in IT runbook with explicit client-side steps. Long-term: network will add automated MSS clamp on all internal egress/load-balancer paths and update onboarding doc to recommend MTU-aware VPN configs. Follow-up task created to track firmware-level vendor escalation for common consumer models.
